explanation:
The rule here is simple enough to read straight off the fact sheet, so I'll go directly to the solution.

## What the grids are made of

Each input is an empty 13×13 canvas with just two single cells of colour 2 (the "seeds"). In the output, colour 2 has grown to 48 cells with a bounding box covering the whole grid, and a new colour 1 has appeared in a rectangle in the middle.

## How the output is built from the seeds

The added colour-2 segments in the fact sheet are all full-grid lines: every segment of colour 2 starts or ends at a grid border and stops only at a seed. Putting the pieces together, each seed sends out a complete horizontal line and a complete vertical line through itself. Two seeds give two rows and two columns, which cross like a tic-tac-toe grid. Counting agrees: 13 + 13 cells per cross, 26 × 2 = 52, minus 4 crossing points counted twice = 48 cells of colour 2 — exactly what the fact sheet reports.

The colour-1 region is the rectangle enclosed by the two rows and two columns. In pair 1 the seeds sit at rows 4 and 8, columns 2 and 10; the 1s occupy rows 5–7 and columns 3–9, i.e. strictly between the lines, bounding box [5,3,7,9] of size 3×7 = 21 cells. In pair 2 the seeds are at rows 3 and 9, columns 3 and 8; the 1s fill rows 4–8, columns 4–7 (5×4 = 20 cells). Both match the fact sheet exactly, so the rule is:

1. Draw a full row and a full column of the seed colour through each seed.
2. Fill the open rectangle strictly inside the two rows and two columns with colour 1.

Nothing in the rule depends on where the seeds are relative to each other (which one is higher or further left), only on the sorted rows and columns, so it generalises to any pair of seeds.

## Applying it to the test input

The test seeds are at (1,4) and (10,9). So we draw rows 1 and 10 and columns 4 and 9 in colour 2, then fill rows 2–9, columns 5–8 with colour 1 (an 8×4 block of 32 cells). The construction stages I emit are: the two crosses (one per seed), then the interior fill, then the final canvas.
code:
def transform(grid):
    g = np.array(grid)
    bg = background(g)
    out = g.copy()
    h, w = g.shape

    # seeds: the non-background cells
    ys, xs = np.where(g != bg)
    seeds = list(zip(ys.tolist(), xs.tolist()))
    colour = int(g[seeds[0]])

    # stage 1: a full row and a full column through each seed
    for (y, x) in seeds:
        out[y, :] = colour
        out[:, x] = colour
        emit(out, f"draw full row {y} and column {x} of colour {colour} through seed ({y},{x})")

    # stage 2: fill the rectangle strictly between the lines with colour 1
    rows = sorted(y for y, _ in seeds)
    cols = sorted(x for _, x in seeds)
    y0, y1 = rows[0] + 1, rows[-1]
    x0, x1 = cols[0] + 1, cols[-1]
    if y1 > y0 and x1 > x0:
        out[y0:y1, x0:x1] = 1
    emit(out, f"fill the interior rectangle rows {y0}-{y1-1}, cols {x0}-{x1-1} with colour 1")

    emit(out, "final canvas")
    return out
